description: External GPU end-to-end validation matrix for loading and quantization roadmap task 8. Entries are plans, not results.
rationale: Cases written by hand because their expected outcome is a claim about the world rather than about the code: which archs AITER builds FP4 kernels for, which torch versions can shard uint8 MXFP4, which inputs a model needs. A generator reading the same probe functions the runner calls could only assert that the code agrees with itself. These win any collision with a generated case, so their IDs and result history stay stable.
sampling_rationale: How a model is sampled belongs to the model, not to the matrix. A single default was applied to every model here, and it was Z-Image-Turbo's: four steps at 512x512 with whatever guidance the runner defaulted to. Turbo is distilled to run that way, so its cases looked fine and hid the problem. Base Z-Image is a fifty-step CFG model, and at four steps it returned a blurry blob that no comparison against it could mean anything, which is how a quality gate came to be calibrated on unconverged images. Settings are therefore per model and copied from this repo's own benchmark configs rather than chosen here. A model with no entry cannot be run: an image produced at the wrong operating point is worse than no image, because it looks like a result. Where a model has no config of its own, the settings its runner declares in DefaultInputValues are used instead and the entry says so; that is still the model's own statement of how it runs, and for Krea-2-Turbo the runner enforces it. Only two things here are chosen rather than read: the prompt, which is an input rather than an operating point, and the input image, which is the file the model's own config passes.

sampling_gaps: Models still without settings: CausalWan, which has no weights on any machine this has run on, so filling it in would record an operating point nobody could check. FLUX.2-klein-4B, Cosmos3-Nano and Cosmos3-Super were in that position until their weights were fetched onto the gfx950 node; each now carries its runner's own declared operating point, since none of the three is named by a benchmark config. Withheld models were said to need none, since their cases assert a rejection and never reach a sampler, but that was wrong: an entry is looked up while the command is being built, so a rejection case for a model without one reported that it could not run and asserted nothing. The seven withheld models whose weights are on the gfx950 node now carry entries taken from their runners' declarations. Still without one: CausalWan, SD3.5, LTX-2 and the two other HunyuanVideo 1.5 variants, whose checkpoints are not cached anywhere this has run, and Wan2.2-Distilled-I2V, whose base repo is cached but whose distilled state dicts are not. A model with no entry refuses to run rather than borrowing another model's settings.
video_scoring_note: Video entries carry num_frames and render a clip. The blank-output gate reads those clips and fails a uniform frame, so a collapsed video cannot pass, but the SSIM comparison against a reference is not applied to video: it compares one still against another, and no video model here has been shown to reproduce a clip frame for frame across a numeric change. Their scores would be observations of which sample came out, which is the same reason the image comparison only decides Z-Image-Turbo.

cases.quality_notes: Compare text fidelity and composition against the bf16 case with the same seed. This one genuinely needs the arch: _use_aiter_fp8_rdna4 routes FP8 through AITER's quantizer and layer layout only on gfx1200 or gfx1201, so no amount of gfx950 FP8 covers it.

Confirm the logged Transformers 4 text-encoder fallback is post-load, then compare to the Transformers 5 result. This asked for RDNA4 and an offload mode as well, which confounded three factors: what it tests is a library, feature-detected on whether transformers.core_model_loading imports, and nothing about it is architectural. Pinned here instead, where it records an environment mismatch until a Transformers 4 environment exists, which is the requirement it actually has.

Sequential offload moving submodules to the host between calls, with an FP8 transformer, on the torchao backend this arch selects. Sequential offload is an accelerate hook with no platform gate, so waiting for RDNA4 to test it left it untested everywhere. Ran first at two ranks, inherited from the RDNA4 case this replaces, and NCCL refused with a duplicate GPU: accelerate places the offloaded modules on the default device for every rank, so both ranks landed on one device and the first all-to-all failed. One rank is where this belongs, since offload exists to fit a model that does not fit; the multi-rank combination has no owner and should be refused rather than left to fail at the collective.

expected.error_pattern: MXFP4 packed weight cannot be placed under FSDP2|177948

cases.quality_notes: Inspect both transformer phases; transformer_2 is expected to remain FP8. Now expects the refusal rather than success, because the equivalent case ran on gfx950 and met the MXFP4 FSDP2 gate; on torch 2.12 or newer both flip back to success. The high-precision step count is required: --use_hybrid_gemm_schedule refuses to run without it, so as written this case would have failed on that rather than on anything it means to test, wherever it ran. What is left that is specific to this arch is the pairing of AITER FP8 with AITER MXFP4; the mixed schedule itself is covered on gfx950 by rocm-flux2-hybrid-eager and rocm-wan22-t2v-hybrid-fsdp4. The success expectation still needs checking against the MXFP4 FSDP2 gate: the FP4 half targets transformer.blocks, which the strategy also wraps, so validate_format_fsdp_placement is required and refuses unless torch carries pytorch/pytorch#177948 (2.12). On an older torch expect a preflight_failure instead.

cases.coverage_note: What remains specific to this arch is AITER's FP4 kernels as built for gfx1200/gfx1201; the group offload half is covered on gfx950 by rocm-krea2-fp4-eager-group-offload, so this is no longer the only thing standing between the project and any offload coverage.

cases.quality_notes: Written expecting success and run: the hook pins each tensor before onloading it and torch has no pin_memory for Float4_e2m1fn_x2, so it raised from inside the offload rather than from anything this project owns. Now refused before allocation, which is what this asserts. Replaces a Cosmos3-Super hybrid case pinned to RDNA4, where a 128G transformer at two ranks was an expensive way to reach the same host-memory flag.

Whole-model offload with both the transformer and the text encoder quantized, which is where a quantized module moved between devices can lose its scales. Replaces the same combination pinned to Hopper and to RDNA4; FP8 on CUDA stays covered by ada-flux1-fp8-eager-te, and the ROCm INT8 refusal the RDNA4 slot asserted is platform-level, already proven by rocm-zimage-int8-rejected.

Expected rejection must precede reads of the external LightX2V state dicts. Blocked before hardware: this model has no sampling entry, and an entry is read while the command is built, so on an RDNA4 node this reports that it cannot run and asserts nothing. Its base repo is cached on the gfx950 node but the distilled state dicts are not, so no operating point can be checked there either.

The composition adapter has no standard meta-construction seam. Blocked before hardware: SD3.5 has no sampling entry and no cached checkpoint on any node this has run on, so booking an RDNA4 box for it would report that it cannot run. The refusal itself is not architectural and would hold wherever the weights are.

The manual single-file fallback is intentionally excluded from collective loading. Blocked before hardware: CausalWan has no sampling entry and no cached checkpoint anywhere this has run, so this reports that it cannot run rather than asserting the refusal. Not architectural either; it would hold on any node holding the weights.

FSDP cannot safely apply the Transformers 4 text-encoder post-load fallback. The refusal is decided by whether the installed Transformers carries the streaming loader, not by the accelerator, so this no longer asks for RDNA4: it records an environment mismatch until a Transformers 4 environment exists, and asserting it there tests the torchao path this arch actually selects.

Narrowed from non_rdna4_rocm to gfx942: _AITER_FP4_UNSUPPORTED_ARCHS names only gfx942, so this rejection is that arch's behaviour rather than all of non-RDNA4 ROCm. gfx950 accepts FP4 and is covered by rocm-gfx950-flux2-fp4-eager. FLUX.2-dev is a gated repo, so a run needs hub auth; a 401 previously matched the rejection pattern and was mis-scored.

First FP4 success expected on ROCm outside RDNA4. probe_format_backend_capabilities on gfx950 reports aiter_mxfp4 available with no reason, where gfx942 refuses it because AITER compiles no Float4_e2m1fn_x2 kernels for that arch. Predicted from the probe; not yet run.

Replicated meta load does not shard, so the packed MXFP4 weight never reaches FSDP2 and the torch limitation that blocks the fsdp_blockwise case does not apply. Text encoder stays unquantized by declaration.

Still rejected on gfx950, but for the torch version rather than the architecture: MXFP4 packs two 4-bit values into a uint8, and FSDP2 before pytorch/pytorch#177948 (torch 2.12) cannot shard a non-floating-point parameter. This image carries 2.9.1. Krea-2 quantizes transformer.transformer_blocks and wraps the same blocks for FSDP, so the placement check is required and fires. Expect this case to flip to inference_success on a torch 2.12 image.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserHunyuanvideo15SparseModel does not support replicated_meta materialization.*sparse blocks outside _build_transformer

cases.quality_notes: Composing base non-block weights with remapped Tencent sparse blocks happens outside the transformer seam, so the refusal has to come from the preflight rather than from the composition failing later. Replicated rather than sharded because the sharded flag never reaches the load declaration for this family: the capability gate refuses it first, which rocm-hunyuan15-sparse-fsdp-flag-refused pins separately. A sparse attention backend is named because this runner refuses to run without one, which would otherwise be the failure this case recorded.

The HunyuanVideo 1.5 runners declare no fully_shard_degree capability at all, so the sharding flag is refused while the config is validated, before any load contract is selected. Asserted separately from the withheld reason because it is an earlier and stronger refusal: it holds however the load declaration later changes.

Group offload against quantized weights that can actually move: FP8 rather than the FP4 the group hook cannot pin or place. Keeps a positive result for this offload mode, so the two FP4 rejections next to it are read as a limit of AITER FP4 rather than of group offloading.

The mixed FP8/FP4 schedule, keeping the first and last denoising step in the higher precision. Pinned to gfx950 rather than to the arch pair, for the same reason FP4 is: AITER ships no FP4 kernels for gfx942. The mixed schedule had no coverage anywhere while its three cases waited on RDNA4 and Blackwell, and none of them passed the step count the schedule requires.

expected.error_pattern: MXFP4 packed weight cannot be placed under FSDP2|177948

cases.quality_notes: The mixed schedule against the blockwise fill and a two-phase transformer, which is the same combination rdna4-wan22-hybrid-fsdp asks for. Written expecting success and run: refused, because this torch cannot shard a non-floating-point parameter under FSDP2 and the FP4 half targets the blocks the strategy wraps. That is the gate the RDNA4 case's own notes predicted, now measured rather than guessed, and it flips to a success expectation on torch 2.12 or newer, which carries pytorch/pytorch#177948. Each result records the torch it ran against, so which side of that line a run sits on stays readable.

The densest part of the AITER FP8 path and the one an RDNA4 booking is actually for: per-block quantization during the fill, plus the AITER Transformers streaming adapter for the text encoder, neither of which any other case reaches. The rest of the RDNA4 set was eager, or quantized the transformer alone, so this hole was invisible while the whole group sat unrun.
